standard_prerequisites.name: Additivity of divisors for a restricted family
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter chow.tex, label lemma-additivity-divisors-restricted, invoked at proof line 3536
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the final identity comparing length_A(M/tM) with the sum over the minimal primes of Ass(M) of the residue length times the local length, which is where the coefficient comparison ends.

core_obligations: Write [F]_{k+1} = sum n_i [W_i] over the irreducible components of the support of delta-dimension k + 1, note the family is locally finite, and reduce the lemma to the two coefficientwise identities [F_0]_k = sum n_i[(W_i)_0]_k and the same for the fibre at infinity, since the family lemma then gives the rational equivalence (proof lines 3490-3505).

Fix an integral closed Z' of delta-dimension k with generic point xi' and set xi = (xi', 0) in X times_S P^1_S; from assumption (3) deduce that xi is not an associated point of F, so that M = F_xi is a Cohen-Macaulay module over A = O_{X times P^1, xi} of support dimension one (proof lines 3507-3519).

Use assumption (2) to see that dim(Supp(M/tM)) = 0, hence that the coordinate t cutting out X times D_0 is a nonzerodivisor on M, identify the W_i through xi with the minimal primes q_i of Ass(M) with multiplicities length_{A_{q_i}} M_{q_i}, and compare the coefficient n = length_A(M/tM) with m = sum length_A(A/(t, q_i)A) length_{A_{q_i}} M_{q_i}, which are equal by the additivity lemma (proof lines 3520-3537).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to coefficientwise identities on the two fibres (proof lines 3490-3505).
Turn the coefficient comparison into a statement about one Cohen-Macaulay module over a two-dimensional local ring (proof lines 3507-3519).
Use that the local equation of the fibre is a nonzerodivisor and apply the additivity lemma (proof lines 3520-3537).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for a coherent sheaf F on X times P^1 whose support has dimension at most k + 1, with both fibres over zero and infinity of dimension at most k and with no embedded associated point of dimension at least k inside those fibres, the two fibre cycle classes are rationally equivalent on X (statement lines 3469-3487, tag 02S6). The proof reduces to a coefficient comparison and then does genuine local algebra: at the generic point of a component of the fibre it must use the absence of embedded associated points to conclude that the local module is Cohen-Macaulay, then use the dimension bound on the fibre to see that the coordinate cutting out the fibre is a nonzerodivisor, and finally match length_A(M/tM) with a sum over the minimal primes of the associated primes by an additivity statement. The local algebra is the substance, so the claim is H2.
